quotes.text: Teams isn't the vault. It's the lobby. The vault lives in conditional access, purview DLP, Entra ID governance, and share point sharing limits.

quotes.text: Most people think a private channel means private. We know better. Private just means different plumbing. New site collection, new permission surface.

quotes.text: Now we need truth. Cold timestamp. Signed by the system. Enable the unified audit log. If it's off, nothing exists. No retroactive memory.

takeaways: Teams is only the front end; real protection lives in Conditional Access, Purview DLP, Entra ID Governance and SharePoint sharing settings, and private channels add separate SharePoint sites that need their own governance.

Enforce MFA for everyone including guests, block legacy authentication, require compliant devices or app protection, and put DLP with policy tips and override justification on Teams chat and channels.
Guests must expire through access reviews and time-bound access packages, and the unified audit log, retention policies and legal hold provide the evidence trail you need when something goes wrong.
hook: Microsoft Teams channels are not secure by default: guests linger, private channels spawn hidden SharePoint sites and pasted PII travels far beyond the chat. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins and security teams who need a concrete hardening plan for hybrid, guest-heavy tenants. Walk away with a five-layer playbook covering Conditional Access, Purview DLP, guest lifecycle governance, audit and retention that you can test in your own tenant.
